text:
Maya: heads-up — after the kernel-selector tweak on main i'm seeing a p95 tokens/sec regression (~30%) for tp=2 seq=8192 with FP8 weights + INT8 output quantizer. trace=1812607777

Sam: repro command + trace? paste bench invocation

Maya: `python -m rdinfer.bench --tp=2 --pp=1 --seq_len=8192 --batch=1 --dtype=fp8 --quantizer=int8` and nvprof attached. NVTX shows a kernel swap at iter ~118 then large AllReduce waits.

Maya: perf excerpt:
```
[117] GEMM=sgemv_fp8    time=0.92ms  overlap=0.48
[118] GEMM=sgemm_q_v2  time=1.80ms  sync_scale=1.08ms
[119] AllReduce_wait   44.5ms  overlap_ratio=0.11
KV_cache_hit_rate   0.95 -> 0.69 around layer boundary
```

Rohan: selector likely flipped tiling/kernel. what do kernel scores look like for that layer?

Maya: selector log: `[selector] layer=27 seq=8192 candidates=[sgemv_fp8, sgemm_q_v2, sgemm_small] scores=[0.50,0.53,0.42] chosen=sgemm_q_v2` — tiny margin

Ali: note: sgemm_q_v2 emits an extra synchronous scale/dequant op on the default stream. that op can block NCCL overlap. our cost model doesn't account for that.

Nina: can you isolate fp8 vs int8 path? try pure fp16 and fp8-only runs

Maya: fp16 baseline OK. fp8-only loses ~10%. the big regression happens when fp8 weights + int8 quantizer are used (output scaling path)

Sam: set `REDWOOD_KERNEL_DEBUG=1` and `REDWOOD_KV_DEBUG=1` and upload logs

Maya: did that. kernel switch + kv miss spike co-occur. i suspect attention-kernel ordering differs for that GEMM variant and we miss a KV reuse on a shard boundary.

Jess: quick mitigation: can you force the previous kernel for that layer and measure? if it recovers we can pin via rollout rule

Maya: forced `sgemv_fp8` for layer 27 via env override; p95 recovered to within 5% of baseline. so kernel choice is dominant.

Ali: proposed fixes:
- add synthetic penalty to selector for kernels that require a sync-scale/dequant step
- add TP-boundary penalty when tiling increases allreduce window or misaligns shard slices

Rohan: also check whether tiling misaligns tensor slices across TP shards leading to larger NCCL messages and worse schedule

Maya: simplified timeline:
| compute-GEMM(1.8ms) | sync-scale(1.08ms) | AllReduce(44ms, poor overlap) |

Nina: KV miss-rate drop might be a small bug where that kernel variant writes/reads KV in a different layout or ordering. i'll audit attention->kv ordering and prefix reuse logic on kernel-switch paths

Sam: where are traces? nvprof tar and rdinfer trace bundle?

Rohan: uploaded `/tmp/1812607777-nvprof.tar.gz` and trace bundle to https://redwood.internal/traces/1812607777 (logs attached)

perf-bot: @channel regression alert: p95 tokens/sec degraded 31% for tp=2 seq=8192. auto-incident triggered per SLO

Jess: i'll push a rollback rule to pin layer=27 to `sgemv_fp8` on canary fleet. ETA ~15m

Ali: i'll prototype selector patch that: (a) accounts for synchronous scale/dequant cost, (b) models TP-boundary comm penalty, (c) includes a unit test with the bench config

Nina: once ali has a branch i'll run the KV cache audit against it; they may interact

Rohan: i'll add a tiny reproducer toggling tiling flags and upload NVTX timeline variants. ETA EOD

Sam: after ali's patch we should run an A/B with `--live-rollout=canary` and collect token-level metrics + kv hit-rates

Maya: debugging notes: use `REDWOOD_KERNEL_DEBUG=1` and `REDWOOD_KV_DEBUG=1` and add NVTX markers around attention+kv writes. those helped pin the miss spike

Jess: rollback pushed to canary; posting compare numbers in ~10m

Maya: thanks all. flagging for runtime sync tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
